description:
Two family producing-closure generators have no check mode, so the CI contract's family-closure check skips them and their closures can go stale unnoticed; every family closure is checked.

## Background

`dev/scripts/check-family-producing-closures.py` runs the `--check` mode of every live generator named `make-*-producing-inputs.py` that offers one. `dev/active/1d4fd63d/make-external-producing-inputs.py` writes `external-producing-inputs.json`, and `dev/active/c04dd4ac-zen3-shifts-and-permutations/survey/make-shift-producing-inputs.py` writes `shift-profile-producing-inputs.json` beside it; each writes its output on every invocation, to a default path or to its first argument, and offers no `--check`. The dense and logical generators of the mid-range study show the form: `--check` writes nothing and exits non-zero when the committed closure differs from the tree.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: Each of the two generators has a `--check` mode that writes nothing and exits non-zero when its committed closure differs from the tree, shown by a test on a fixture where an enumerated source is added.
- [hard] REQ-02: The family-closure check of the CI contract runs both generators' checks without an edit of the CI script, and reports the number of closures it checked.
- [hard] REQ-03: Both checks pass on the committed tree, or a closure that is stale is regenerated by its generator; no committed receipt, receipt input snapshot, trial ledger or frozen addendum changes.

## Notes

Found while adding the family-closure check to the CI contract.
